results.title: Enhancing QUIC: Quality-of-Service LLM Serving and MASQUE Proxy Scheduling
KV Cache Compression Based on Token-Level Redundancy Elimination and Bit-Level Encoding
results.venue: International Conference on Artificial Intelligence Circuits and Systems
results.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) face storage and access limitations during development, requiring extensive reads of key-value (KV) cache data for each token generation. This paper designs a hardware-friendly lossless compression and decompression method for KV cache based on Token-level Redundancy Elimination and Bit-level Encoding (TREBE), reducing the amount of KV cache data that needs to be stored. In detail, token-level redundancy is first eliminated by performing subtraction between the same layers of different tokens, followed by bit-level encoding using XOR and bit-plane techniques. TREBE achieves an average compression ratio of 2.1x for the KV cache of LLaMA2-7B and OPT-6.7B models on the WikiText2 and C4 datasets, representing a 1.9x improvement over Huffman coding. With the support of TSMC 28nm process, TREBE operates at 0.9V and 0.8GHz, achieving a throughput of 6.38GB/s. Compared to Huffman coding, energy efficiency is improved by 10x, and area efficiency is enhanced by 31.2x.

Computationally Efficient FPGA-based Large Language Model Inference for Real-Time Decision-Making in Robotic Systems
results.venue: IEEE/RJS International Conference on Intelligent RObots and Systems
results.abstract: Integrating Large Language Models (LLMs) into modern robotic systems presents significant computational and energy constraint challenges, particularly for human-centered robotic applications. This paper presents a novel hardware optimization technique for deploying LLMs on resource-constrained embedded devices, achieving an up to 77% reduction in computational latency through an FPGA implementation in comparison to other popular embedded computing devices (e.g., CPU and GPUs). Additionally, we demonstrate our methodology by deploying a LLaMA 2-7B model on a Unitree Go2 robotic dog integrated with the proposed FPGA platform. The proposed optimization framework preserves real-time interaction capabilities while significantly reducing computational and energy overhead, facilitating efficient natural language processing for human-robot interaction in safety-critical and dynamic environments. Experimental results demonstrate that the FPGA-based LLaMA 2-7B implementation achieves up to 6.06-fold and 1.95-fold higher throughput compared to baseline CPU and GPU implementations while maintaining comparable inference accuracy. Furthermore, the proposed FPGA design surpasses existing state-of-the-art FPGA implementations, delivering a 30% improvement in computational efficiency.
